raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview Refs #63519. This change proposes delaying deferred block reclamation by one processed step when speculative decoding is enabled, so the completion fence covers draft KV writes issued after the output-copy event. **Open for review. Runtime correctness and performance validation evidence remain outstanding.** ## Claims - Adds an extra-step fence for speculative decoding while retaining the existing non-speculative fence. - Adds a device-synchronized drain for deferred blocks on idle and stalled engine paths. - Adds scheduler and drain contract tests. Their presence is not a claim that the tests have passed. ## Validation Submission revision: `50f6d41b5660672280367ff41850f023233be156`; implementation base: `256d8b40d0864aa694e3dc236d9b351886a4a94a`. The submission review inspected the diff and the scheduler, engine batch-queue, executor RPC and worker synchronization code. No runtime test was executed in that review, and no original RED/GREEN logs have been verified for this revision. The added executor fixture records calls; it does not validate GPU stream or RDMA ordering. Planned CPU regression command (not yet executed in the submission review): ```sh .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py -q ``` Remaining validation items: - Record a failing baseline reproducer and passing candidate tests, including abort/preemption, outstanding batches, synchronization failure and idle/stall drain behavior. - Run applicable formatting/type checks. DCO is now passing; author metadata and sign-off were corrected without changing the code tree. - Validate the affected speculative-decoding P/D configuration, output correctness and block lifetime; measure synchronization overhead and examine it with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. - Verify compatibility with the updated main base. No GPU/NPU, real-model, RDMA, end-to-end serving or performance result is claimed here. ## Details The problematic sequence is: a request's output-copy event completes; its draft forward can still be writing KV; the scheduler releases its blocks; an unordered receive path may write a new request's KV into the reused blocks. The proposal holds those blocks until a later step's completion, with an explicit synchronized drain when progress would otherwise stop. The design still needs scrutiny: `model_executed=False` does not establish that the batch queue is empty, and the extra fence currently applies to every speculative method rather than only V2 KV-writing speculators. Additional block retention and synchronous drains may affect memory pressure and latency. Issue-number and area-keyword searches found no confirmed equivalent open implementation during the submission review; this is not an exhaustive equivalence proof. This PR presents the proposal for review while completing the checks above. AI assistance was used for review and PR preparation. This PR does not assert completion of the required human end-to-end review or validation. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. Findings remain open above. - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change with meaningful regression and affected-path evidence. - [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Completes configured checks and required documentation. - [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Supports claims with verified runtime evidence and follows the contributing guide.

+def test_spec_decode_defers_free_by_one_extra_step():
+    """Speculative decoding issues its draft forward *after* the step's
+    AsyncOutput copy event is recorded (so the D2H copy can overlap the
+    proposal), so a finished request's blocks may still be written by the
+    draft model of the step that produced its final token. Those writes are
+    only known complete once the next step's output has been processed, so
+    the blocks must be held one step longer.
+    """
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(model=MODEL, num_speculative_tokens=3)
+    scheduler.defer_block_free = True
+    pool = scheduler.kv_cache_manager.block_pool
+    num_free_initially = pool.get_num_free_blocks()
+
+    short, long = create_requests(
+        num_requests=2,
+        num_tokens=NUM_PROMPT_TOKENS,
+        max_tokens=20,
+        stop_token_ids=[STOP_TOKEN_ID],
+        req_ids=["short", "long"],
+    )
+    scheduler.add_request(short)
+    scheduler.add_request(long)
+
+    out0 = scheduler.schedule()
+    step_seq = scheduler.sched_step_seq
+    num_free_running = pool.get_num_free_blocks()
+    assert num_free_running < num_free_initially
+
+    # "short" stops on step 1's output while step 1's draft forward may
+    # still be writing its KV blocks.
+    scheduler.update_from_output(
+        out0,
+        _make_model_runner_output_with_tokens(
+            out0, {"short": STOP_TOKEN_ID, "long": 0}
+        ),
+    )
+    assert short.is_finished()
+    assert len(scheduler.deferred_frees) == 1
+    # Fence is one step past the step whose draft forward writes the blocks.
+    assert scheduler.deferred_frees[0][0] == step_seq + 1
+    held_blocks = len(scheduler.deferred_frees[0][1])
+    assert pool.get_num_free_blocks() == num_free_running
+
+    # Step 2 is dispatched after step 1's draft forward, so processing its
+    # output fences the draft writes and the blocks return to the pool.
+    out1 = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert long.request_id in out1.num_scheduled_tokens
+    scheduler.update_from_output(out1, _make_model_runner_output(out1))
+    assert not scheduler.deferred_frees
+    assert pool.get_num_free_blocks() == num_free_running + held_blocks
+
+
+def test_block_write_fence_unchanged_without_spec_decode():
+    """The extra fence step only applies when speculative decoding can issue
+    draft KV writes; the non-speculative path keeps its original fence."""

+    spec_scheduler = create_scheduler(model=MODEL, num_speculative_tokens=3)
+    assert spec_scheduler.num_spec_tokens == 3
+    assert spec_scheduler._block_write_fence_seq(7) == 8

+
+class _RecordingExecutor:
+    """Minimal stand-in for the engine's executor, recording RPC calls."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.calls: list[str] = []
+
+    def collective_rpc(self, method, timeout=None, args=(), kwargs=None):
+        self.calls.append(method)
+        return [None]

+
+def _make_idle_core(scheduler):
+    """Attach the scheduler/executor pair an idle `EngineCore` would have."""
+    from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+    from vllm.v1.engine.core import EngineCore
+
+    core = SimpleNamespace(scheduler=scheduler, model_executor=_RecordingExecutor())
+    core._flush_deferred_frees = lambda: EngineCore._flush_deferred_frees(core)
+    return core
+
+
+def test_idle_engine_flushes_deferred_frees():
+    """When the engine drains there is no later step to advance the fence, so
+    the idle path synchronizes the device and returns the held blocks."""
+    from vllm.v1.engine.core import EngineCore
+
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(model=MODEL, num_speculative_tokens=3)
+    scheduler.defer_block_free = True
+    pool = scheduler.kv_cache_manager.block_pool
+    num_free_initially = pool.get_num_free_blocks()
+
+    short, long = create_requests(
+        num_requests=2,
+        num_tokens=NUM_PROMPT_TOKENS,
+        max_tokens=20,
+        stop_token_ids=[STOP_TOKEN_ID],
+        req_ids=["short", "long"],
+    )
+    scheduler.add_request(short)
+    scheduler.add_request(long)
+    out0 = scheduler.schedule()
+    scheduler.update_from_output(
+        out0,
+        _make_model_runner_output_with_tokens(
+            out0, {"short": STOP_TOKEN_ID, "long": 0}
+        ),
+    )
+
+    # "short" finished, but its blocks are held one extra step.
+    assert short.is_finished()
+    assert scheduler.has_deferred_frees()
+    held_blocks = len(scheduler.deferred_frees[0][1])
+    num_free_held = pool.get_num_free_blocks()
+    assert num_free_held < num_free_initially
+
+    core = _make_idle_core(scheduler)
+    EngineCore._flush_deferred_frees(core)
+
+    # The device is fenced before the blocks go back to the pool.
+    assert core.model_executor.calls == ["synchronize_device"]
+    assert not scheduler.has_deferred_frees()
+    assert pool.get_num_free_blocks() == num_free_held + held_blocks
+
+    # Idempotent: a second idle pass does no extra work.
+    EngineCore._flush_deferred_frees(core)
+    assert core.model_executor.calls == ["synchronize_device"]
+
+
+def test_idle_engine_skips_sync_without_deferred_frees():
+    """The idle path must not add a device synchronization on every idle
+    iteration; it only runs while blocks are actually held."""
+    from vllm.v1.engine.core import EngineCore

+    core = _make_idle_core(scheduler)
+    EngineCore._flush_deferred_frees(core)

+    scheduler.add_request(long)

+    scheduler.update_from_output(
+        out0,
+        _make_model_runner_output_with_tokens(
+            out0, {"short": STOP_TOKEN_ID, "long": 0}
+        ),
+    )
+    assert short.is_finished()
+    assert scheduler.has_deferred_frees()
+    held_blocks = len(scheduler.deferred_frees[0][1])
+    num_free_held = pool.get_num_free_blocks()
+
+    core = _make_idle_core(scheduler)
+    core.step_fn = lambda: (None, False)
+    core.post_step = lambda model_executed: None
+    core.output_queue = None
+    EngineCoreProc._process_engine_step(core)
+
+    assert core.model_executor.calls == ["synchronize_device"]
+    assert not scheduler.has_deferred_frees()
+    assert pool.get_num_free_blocks() == num_free_held + held_blocks
